evals.name: api-status-regression-between-tags
evals.prompt: Our checkout service's `POST /payments` endpoint started returning 500s last sprint. Commit `a1b2c3d` (tag `v2.1.0`) is known-good: the same request returns `201 Created` with a payment id. Commit `9f8e7d6` (tag `v2.2.0`, current HEAD) is known-bad: the same request returns `500 Internal Server Error`. I can reproduce with `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/payments -d '{"amount":100}'`. There are about 45 commits between the tags. Walk me through finding the exact commit that introduced the regression.

assertions.text: Uses git bisect (start, bad, good) rather than manually checking out commits one by one
Marks the known-good commit a1b2c3d as good and the known-bad commit 9f8e7d6 as bad
Uses the curl command as the reproduction test at each bisect step
After bisect identifies the first bad commit, instructs reading its diff to find the bug
Includes git bisect reset at the end

evals.name: automated-unit-test-bisect
evals.prompt: The unit test `test_discount_code_lowercase` fails on `main` at commit `z9y8x7w` but passes on the release branch at commit `m1n2o3p`. I have a script `./run_test.sh test_discount_code_lowercase` that exits `0` when the test passes and `1` when it fails. There are about 80 commits between the two. I don't want to manually check each one. How do I automate the bisect and what do I do once git names the bad commit?

assertions.text: Uses git bisect run with the test script to automate the bisect
Marks z9y8x7w as bad and m1n2o3p as good
After bisect names the bad commit, instructs reading the diff to find the offending line
Includes git bisect reset after the automated bisect completes
